requirements.title: Git routes and their framing
requirements.rationale: A stock git client speaks to exactly three URLs and reads plain text, so the routes, their content types and the shape of a refusal are the contract every git client depends on.

criteria.condition: an authorized caller sends GET /git/:org/:slug.git/info/refs with service=git-upload-pack and no Git-Protocol header for a ready workspace
criteria.action: answer with the version 0 ref advertisement of the workspace's repository
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; Content-Type application/x-git-upload-pack-advertisement; Cache-Control no-cache; the body starts with the pkt-line '# service=git-upload-pack' followed by a flush packet, then one line per ref, the first of which carries the capability list

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/fetch_test.go: r = get('/git/acme/demo.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack', basic('x', ownerKey)); assert r.status == 200; assert r.header['Content-Type'] == 'application/x-git-upload-pack-advertisement'; assert r.header['Cache-Control'] == 'no-cache'; pkts = pktlines(r.body); assert pkts[0] == '# service=git-upload-pack\n'; assert pkts[1] is flush; assert some pkt contains 'refs/heads/main'

criteria.condition: an authorized caller sends POST /git/:org/:slug.git/git-upload-pack with a git upload-pack request for a ready workspace
criteria.action: run the fetch exchange on the workspace's repository and stream git's response as it is produced
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; Content-Type application/x-git-upload-pack-result; Cache-Control no-cache; the body is git's upload-pack response; the first bytes of the response reach the client before the git process has ended

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/fetch_test.go: body = a version 0 request built by the test that wants the head of main and says done; r = post('/git/acme/demo.git/git-upload-pack', body, basic('x', ownerKey)); assert r.status == 200; assert r.header['Content-Type'] == 'application/x-git-upload-pack-result'; assert r.header['Cache-Control'] == 'no-cache'; assert r.body contains the bytes 'PACK'; a second case replaces the git runner by one that writes 'NAK' and then blocks on a channel: assert the client reads 'NAK' while the runner is still blocked

criteria.condition: a caller who passed authentication, scope and access sends GET info/refs whose first service value is neither git-upload-pack nor git-receive-pack, or sends none
criteria.action: refuse the request without running git
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with the text body 'invalid or missing service parameter'; a query 'service=git-upload-pack&service=git-receive-pack' is not refused and is answered as upload-pack (Content-Type application/x-git-upload-pack-advertisement)

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/routes_test.go, a table over queries {'' , 'service=', 'service=git-archive', 'service=upload-pack', 'svc=git-upload-pack'}: r = get('/git/acme/demo.git/info/refs?' + q, basic('x', ownerKey)); assert r.status == 400; assert r.body == 'invalid or missing service parameter\n'; assert the git runner was not called; then q = 'service=git-upload-pack&service=git-receive-pack': assert r.status == 200 and r.header['Content-Type'] == 'application/x-git-upload-pack-advertisement'

criteria.action: for any request to one of the three git routes, accept a body larger than [server].max_body_size and a Content-Type that is not application/json, applying neither the REST body limit nor the REST content-type rule
criteria.contract: a POST to git-upload-pack whose body is larger than [server].max_body_size and whose Content-Type is application/x-git-upload-pack-request is not answered 413 or 415

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/routes_test.go: the server of internal/server is built with max_body_size 1024 and the git routes mounted; body = a valid version 0 upload-pack request padded with 4096 bytes of repeated 'have' lines for unknown ids; r = post('/git/acme/demo.git/git-upload-pack', body, basic('x', ownerKey), contentType='application/x-git-upload-pack-request'); assert r.status == 200; control: a POST of 4096 bytes to a REST route of the same server is answered 413

criteria.action: for any refusal decided before the git exchange starts, answer with the HTTP status, Content-Type text/plain; charset=utf-8 and a body of exactly one line holding the message, never the JSON error envelope
criteria.contract: the body is the message followed by one newline; the body does not parse as JSON; statuses and messages are those of the refusals table: 401 'authentication required', 403 'user is blocked', 429 'rate limit exceeded', 404 'repository not found', 403 'token lacks scope git:read', 403 'token lacks scope git:write', 403 'org members have read-only access to this workspace; create a task fork to contribute', 400 'invalid or missing service parameter', 409 'repository not available: workspace is <status>', 409 'repository not available: parent workspace is busy', 409 'repository is read-only: parent workspace is archived', 500 'internal error'

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/routes_test.go, a table with one request per row of the contract's list (each built from the fixtures the other tests of this package use): assert r.status == row.status; assert r.header['Content-Type'] == 'text/plain; charset=utf-8'; assert r.body == row.message + '\n'; assert json.parse(r.body) fails

criteria.condition: a lookup in the store or the opening of the repository fails before the git exchange starts
criteria.action: refuse the request and never report the failure's detail to the caller
criteria.contract: HTTP 500 with the text body 'internal error'; the body holds no path, no SQL text and no error text of the failure; the failure is logged

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/routes_test.go, a table over failures {the workspace lookup returns an error, the access decision returns an error, the repository directory of a ready workspace does not exist}: r = get('/git/acme/demo.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack', basic('x', ownerKey)); assert r.status == 500; assert r.body == 'internal error\n'; assert the log buffer holds one error record

requirements.title: HTTP Basic authentication of git requests
requirements.rationale: git can only present a credential it was asked for, so the hub must challenge in the way git understands and must treat the Basic password exactly as it treats a REST credential.

criteria.condition: a git request carries an Authorization header of scheme Basic whose password is a live API key, a live PAT or the admin token
criteria.action: authenticate the caller by the password alone, never consulting the Basic user name
criteria.contract: the request passes authentication for every user name, including an empty one and another user's name; the caller the later checks see is the credential's user, or the admin token

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/auth_test.go, a table over passwords {owner's API key, owner's PAT with git:read, the admin token} x user names {'', 'x-token-auth', 'git', another user's username}: r = get('/git/acme/demo.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack', basic(name, password)); assert r.status == 200

criteria.condition: a git request has no Authorization header, a scheme other than Basic, Basic data that is not valid base64 or has no colon, an empty password, or a password that is an unknown, revoked or expired credential
criteria.action: challenge the client for Basic credentials with one answer for all of these cases
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 with the header WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="parley" and the text body 'authentication required'; the answer is byte-identical for every case, and is the same for an existing and a nonexistent repository

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
a revoked API key and an expired PAT of the owner exist
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/auth_test.go, a table over headers {none, 'Bearer ' + ownerKey, 'Basic !!!', 'Basic ' + b64('nocolon'), basic('x', ''), basic('x', 'parley_abcdefgh_' + 32 wrong chars), basic('x', revokedKey), basic('x', expiredPat)} x paths {'/git/acme/demo.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack', '/git/acme/nosuch.git/git-receive-pack' (POST)}: assert r.status == 401; assert r.header['WWW-Authenticate'] == 'Basic realm="parley"'; assert r.body == 'authentication required\n'

criteria.condition: a git request carries a valid credential of a blocked user
criteria.action: refuse the request without a Basic challenge
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with the text body 'user is blocked'; no WWW-Authenticate header

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/auth_test.go: block the owner; r = get('/git/acme/demo.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack', basic('x', ownerKey)); assert r.status == 403; assert r.body == 'user is blocked\n'; assert r.header['WWW-Authenticate'] == ''

criteria.condition: an authenticated git request is over the request rate limit of its credential
criteria.action: refuse the request before the binding guard, the scope check and repository resolution run
criteria.contract: HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header holding a whole number of seconds of at least 1 and the text body 'rate limit exceeded'; the answer is the same for an existing and a nonexistent repository

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/auth_test.go: the limiter of internal/server is built with 2 requests per minute; send 2 requests with ownerKey and assert neither is 429; a table over third requests {'/git/acme/demo.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack', '/git/acme/nosuch.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack'}: assert r.status == 429; assert int(r.header['Retry-After']) >= 1; assert r.body == 'rate limit exceeded\n'; a request with a wrong password from the same address is still answered 401

requirements.title: Authorization and repository resolution
requirements.rationale: The git surface must grant exactly what the REST surface grants and must not let a caller without access learn which repositories exist.

criteria.action: for any git request, derive the need from the route: write access and the scope git:write for POST git-receive-pack and for info/refs with service=git-receive-pack, read access and the scope git:read for every other request, checking scopes for PATs only and letting git:write satisfy a git:read check
criteria.contract: the admin token and the owner's API key are granted on all three routes; an org member's API key is granted on the two fetch requests; a PAT of the owner with only git:read is granted on the fetch requests; a PAT of the owner with only git:write is granted on fetch and push requests

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
users: owner (owns demo), member (member of org acme, not owner), stranger (no membership); the admin token; workspace solo that has no organization; workspace other in org beta owned by the stranger
the service that runs after the checks is a recorder
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/authorize_test.go, a table over credentials {admin token, owner API key, member API key, owner PAT [git:read], owner PAT [git:write]} x requests {info/refs upload-pack, POST git-upload-pack, info/refs receive-pack, POST git-receive-pack}: granted = the recording service ran with the expected need and caller; assert granted for every cell of the contract and for no other cell of the table

criteria.condition: a git request is authenticated with a PAT that lacks the scope the route needs
criteria.action: refuse the request before repository resolution, so that the answer does not depend on whether the repository exists
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with the text body 'token lacks scope git:read' on a fetch request and 'token lacks scope git:write' on a push request; the same answer for demo, for a nonexistent slug and for a workspace the PAT's user cannot read

criteria.condition: a git request is authenticated with a workspace-bound PAT and names a repository the binding guard does not cover
criteria.action: refuse the request before the scope check, asking the git guard of package 08 (GuardGit) once
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with the text body 'repository not found', also when the PAT lacks every git scope; the guard was asked once with the authenticated caller, the slug as the caller typed it, the method and the matched git route pattern, and it reports its refusal with the surface 'git' itself; with no guard installed every bound PAT gets this answer on every repository

criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with the text body 'repository not found'; status, headers other than Date and body are identical across all the cases, on all three routes, for workspace statuses pending, cloning, ready, failed and archived

requirements.title: Workspace state on git routes
requirements.rationale: A caller who may read a workspace should be told why its repository cannot be served, and a fork must not be written while its parent cannot take the work.

criteria.condition: a caller with the access the route needs addresses a workspace whose status is not ready
criteria.action: refuse the request without running git and name the status
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with the text body 'repository not available: workspace is <status>', where <status> is pending, cloning, failed or archived

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/state_test.go, a table over statuses {pending, cloning, failed, archived} x requests {info/refs upload-pack, POST git-upload-pack, POST git-receive-pack} as owner: assert r.status == 409; assert r.body == 'repository not available: workspace is ' + status + '\n'; assert the git runner was not called

criteria.condition: a caller with access addresses a ready task fork whose parent workspace is in exclusive maintenance
criteria.action: refuse the request on all three routes
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with the text body 'repository not available: parent workspace is busy'

criteria.condition: a caller with write access sends a push request to a ready task fork whose parent workspace is archived
criteria.action: refuse the push request
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with the text body 'repository is read-only: parent workspace is archived' for POST git-receive-pack and for info/refs with service=git-receive-pack; the push processor is not called

criteria.action: keep serving fetch requests from the fork
criteria.contract: info/refs with service=git-upload-pack and POST git-upload-pack on the fork are answered HTTP 200

requirements.title: Fetch protocol
requirements.rationale: Agents start work on large repositories many times a day; they need the modern protocol, shallow history and incremental fetches from an unmodified git.

criteria.condition: a fetch-side request carries the header Git-Protocol with the entry version=2
criteria.action: serve the request under git protocol version 2
criteria.contract: info/refs answers HTTP 200 with a body whose first pkt-line is 'version 2' and that lists the capabilities ls-refs and fetch, with no ref lines; git clone -c protocol.version=2 exits 0

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
stock git runs as a subprocess against the httptest server, with the credential in the URL's userinfo, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, an empty HOME and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/fetch_test.go: r = get(info/refs upload-pack, header 'Git-Protocol: version=2'); assert pktlines(r.body)[0] == 'version 2\n'; assert body has a line starting 'ls-refs' and one starting 'fetch'; assert no pkt contains 'refs/heads/'; then git -c protocol.version=2 clone <url> d; assert exit 0; assert git -C d rev-parse HEAD == head of main; GIT_TRACE_PACKET output of the clone contains 'version 2'

criteria.condition: a fetch-side request carries no Git-Protocol header, or one without the entry version=2
criteria.action: serve the request under git protocol version 0
criteria.contract: info/refs answers with the service line and the ref advertisement; git clone -c protocol.version=0 exits 0 with the same commits as a version 2 clone

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main
stock git runs as a subprocess against the httptest server, with the credential in the URL's userinfo, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, an empty HOME and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/fetch_test.go, a table over headers {none, 'Git-Protocol: version=1', 'Git-Protocol: foo=bar'}: r = get(info/refs upload-pack, header); assert pktlines(r.body)[0] == '# service=git-upload-pack\n'; then git -c protocol.version=0 clone <url> d0; assert exit 0; assert git -C d0 rev-parse HEAD == head of main

criteria.condition: a git client asks for limited or extended history with --depth, --deepen, --shallow-since, --shallow-exclude or --unshallow
criteria.action: send exactly the history the client asked for
criteria.contract: clone --depth 1 yields 1 commit; a following fetch --deepen 1 yields 2; fetch --shallow-since=<date of the second commit> yields the commits from that date on; fetch --shallow-exclude=<tag on the first commit> yields every commit but the first; fetch --unshallow yields all commits and removes the shallow file; each command exits 0

setup: a hub handler from internal/gitserver served through net/http/httptest over a real store, with workspace demo (org acme, status ready, default branch main) whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds two commits on main, extended to four commits on main with commit dates one day apart and tag v0 on the first
stock git runs as a subprocess against the httptest server, with the credential in the URL's userinfo, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, an empty HOME and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitserver/fetch_test.go, under protocol versions {0, 2}: git clone --depth 1 <url> d; assert count(git -C d rev-list HEAD) == 1; git -C d fetch --deepen 1; assert count == 2; git clone --shallow-since=<date2> <url> s; assert count(s) == 3; git clone --shallow-exclude=v0 <url> x; assert count(x) == 3; git -C d fetch --unshallow; assert count(d) == 4; assert not exists(d/.git/shallow)

criteria.condition: a git client that already holds part of the history fetches again
criteria.action: negotiate haves and wants and send only the objects the client lacks
criteria.contract: after one new commit with one new blob is added to the repository, git fetch exits 0, the client's branch equals the new head, and the fetch received 3 objects (one commit, one tree, one blob)

criteria.contract: HTTP 200 and the same response body kind as for the uncompressed request (it carries the pack)

criteria.condition: a POST git-upload-pack request that passed every check has an empty body, a body that is not valid gzip although Content-Encoding says gzip, or a body that is not a git upload-pack request
criteria.action: report the error in-band and send no pack
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/x-git-upload-pack-result; the body holds one pkt-line that starts with 'ERR ': 'ERR empty request' for an empty body, 'ERR invalid gzip body' for invalid gzip, git's own text otherwise; the body holds no 'PACK'

criteria.condition: an upload-pack request runs longer than [git].timeout

criteria.contract: the request ends within 2 seconds after the timeout; when no pack data had been written the body ends with the pkt-line 'ERR request timed out'; the git client exits with a non-zero status; the process started for the request has exited

requirements.title: Partial clone
requirements.rationale: An agent that reads a handful of files should not download every blob of a large repository.

criteria.condition: a git client clones or fetches with the filter blob:none, blob:limit=<n> or tree:<n>
criteria.action: send the history without the objects the filter excludes
criteria.contract: git clone --no-checkout --filter=blob:none exits 0 and the clone holds no blob; --filter=blob:limit=1k exits 0 and the clone lacks the 200 kB blob and holds the small one; --filter=tree:0 exits 0 and the clone holds commits and neither trees nor blobs

criteria.condition: a git client with a partial clone needs an object the filter left out
criteria.action: serve the on-demand fetch of that object by its id
criteria.contract: git checkout main in a blob:none clone exits 0 and the working tree holds big.bin with its full content

requirements.title: Ref advertisement
requirements.rationale: Hub-owned refs carry every version of every change, and a fork must show the parent's branches as they are now; both reach a client only through what the server advertises.

criteria.action: for any fetch-side ref discovery, advertise every ref of the repository, including branches, tags, notes and every ref under refs/parley/, and HEAD as a symbolic ref to the default branch
criteria.contract: git ls-remote lists HEAD, refs/heads/main, refs/heads/dev, refs/tags/v1, refs/notes/commits, refs/parley/changes/1/1 and refs/parley/sandboxes/sb1/main with their ids; git ls-remote --symref shows HEAD as ref: refs/heads/main

criteria.action: send the commits of that ref, while a default clone receives branches and tags only

requirements.title: Push advertisement and hand-over
requirements.rationale: A push starts with the same checks as a fetch; what happens to the pushed refs is decided by the push rules, which need the request handed to them with the caller already established.

criteria.condition: a caller with write access and, for a PAT, the scope git:write sends GET info/refs with service=git-receive-pack for a ready workspace
criteria.action: answer with the push ref advertisement of the repository
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; Content-Type application/x-git-receive-pack-advertisement; Cache-Control no-cache; the body starts with the pkt-line '# service=git-receive-pack'; every ref is listed, including refs under refs/parley/; the capability list holds report-status, side-band-64k, delete-refs, ofs-delta, atomic and push-options

criteria.condition: a POST git-receive-pack request passed authentication, the rate limit, the binding guard, the scope check, access with need write and the state checks

criteria.contract: the processor is called exactly once and receives the authenticated caller with its credential type (pat, api_key or admin_token), its credential id, its user, its access level on the workspace (owner or admin), the binding the guard returned and the PAT's record with its paths when the credential is a PAT, the workspace record and a body from which it reads the bytes the client sent, also when they exceed [server].max_body_size; the client receives the status, headers and body the processor wrote

requirements.title: Request metric and fetch event
requirements.rationale: An operator needs to see how much git traffic the hub serves and refuses, and an owner who asks for it needs a record of who fetched a repository.

criteria.action: for any request to one of the three git routes, add exactly one to the counter parley_git_requests_total with the label service (info-refs, upload-pack or receive-pack) and the label result: refused for an answer of 401, 403 or 404, ok for a served exchange, error for every other answer and for an exchange that ended with a hub ERR packet, a failed git process or a timeout
criteria.contract: after each request the counter of exactly one (service, result) pair is one higher: served info/refs -> (info-refs, ok); served clone POST -> (upload-pack, ok); 401, 403 and 404 answers -> refused under the route's service; 400, 409, 429 and 500 answers -> error; an empty upload-pack body -> (upload-pack, error); a handed-over push -> (receive-pack, <the result the processor reports>)

requirements.title: Credential helper
requirements.rationale: A developer wants plain hub URLs to work in git without typing a credential, and the credential must never be offered to a host that is not the hub.

criteria.condition: git runs parley credential-helper get, the settings hold a hub URL and a credential, and the request read from stdin names the hub URL's scheme, host and port
criteria.action: print the credential for git and exit 0, making no request to the hub
criteria.contract: stdout is exactly the four lines 'protocol=<protocol as given>', 'host=<host as given>', 'username=x-token-auth', 'password=<credential>', each ended by a newline; stderr is empty; exit status 0; no connection is opened

execution_paths.title: A developer clones a workspace with stock git and the credential helper

steps.action: sets credential.<hub URL>.helper to '!parley credential-helper' and runs git clone <hub URL>/git/acme/demo.git
runs parley credential-helper get with the hub's protocol and host on stdin
compares protocol, host and port with its configured hub URL and prints username x-token-auth and the configured API key
repeats the request with HTTP Basic
authenticates the key, applies the rate limit, resolves acme/demo, grants read access, finds the workspace ready and answers with the ref advertisement
streams the pack, counts the two requests it served as ok and the first as refused
writes the clone and checks out the default branch

real_components: the run function of cmd/parleyd with its real router, limiter, credential check, access rule and store
the parley binary built from cmd/parley, called by git as credential helper
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 as test/e2e starts it, with workspace demo in org acme, status ready, whose bare repository holds branch main (3 commits, files a.txt and big.bin of 200 kB), branch dev, tag v1 and the ref refs/parley/changes/1/1
a developer who owns demo, with an API key

the parley binary is built into t.TempDir(); the test's git runs with an empty HOME, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL the hub's URL, PARLEY_API_KEY the key and -c credential.<hub URL>.helper='!<path>/parley credential-helper'
end_state: the clone's HEAD is refs/heads/main at the hub's head of main and the working tree holds a.txt
the clone has origin/dev and tag v1 and no ref under refs/parley/
git clone of the same URL with PARLEY_API_KEY unset exits non-zero
parley_git_requests_total holds (info-refs, refused) >= 1, (info-refs, ok) >= 1 and (upload-pack, ok) >= 1
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/git_test.go: hub = startHub(t); seed demo; code = git(env, 'clone', hub.url + '/git/acme/demo.git', dir); assert code == 0; assert git(dir, 'symbolic-ref', 'HEAD') == 'refs/heads/main'; assert git(dir, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD') == hubHead('main'); assert exists(dir + '/a.txt'); assert git(dir, 'for-each-ref') has refs/remotes/origin/dev and refs/tags/v1 and no 'parley'; assert git(env without PARLEY_API_KEY, 'clone', url, dir2) != 0; assert the counters of the contract

execution_paths.title: An agent fetches from a task fork with a bound token

steps.action: runs git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none of <hub URL>/git/acme/demo--t1.git with a PAT bound to the fork as the Basic password
sends info/refs and then git-upload-pack under protocol version 2 with a deepen and a filter argument
authenticates the PAT, passes the binding guard for demo--t1, checks git:read, resolves the fork, grants read access and finds the fork ready and its parent neither busy nor archived
copies the fork's tracking refs and the version refs of the fork's changes from the parent's repository and serves the shallow, blob-less pack
records parley.git.fetch for demo--t1 with shallow true and filter blob:none, because audit_fetches is true
runs git fetch origin refs/parley/changes/7/1 and receives the first version of its change
runs git ls-remote on the parent's URL with the same token
answers 404 repository not found, because the binding does not cover the parent

real_components: the run function of cmd/parleyd with its real router, credential check, scope check, access rule, store and event log
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 as test/e2e starts it, with workspace demo in org acme, status ready, whose bare repository holds branch main (3 commits, files a.txt and big.bin of 200 kB), branch dev, tag v1 and the ref refs/parley/changes/1/1
fork demo--t1 of demo owned by an org member, its repository borrowing demo's objects and holding its own branch work; refs/parley/changes/7/1 in demo

a fork view that names the tracking refs refs/heads/main and refs/heads/dev and the source change 7, and a guard that covers demo--t1 for the token: the ones of packages 15, 22 and 08 when they are built, otherwise test implementations passed to the run function
a PAT of the member with git:read bound to demo--t1; the setting audit_fetches true on demo--t1
end_state: the clone is shallow (1 commit) and holds no blob before checkout of other commits
origin/main in the clone equals the parent's current head of main, also after the parent's main moved and the agent fetched again
FETCH_HEAD after the version-ref fetch equals the parent's refs/parley/changes/7/1
the event log holds parley.git.fetch events for workspace demo--t1 with actor_type pat, the first with metadata shallow true and filter 'blob:none'
git ls-remote on /git/acme/demo.git with the bound token exited non-zero and its output contains 'repository not found'
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/git_test.go: code = git('clone', '--depth', '1', '--filter=blob:none', forkURL(pat), d); assert code == 0; assert count(git(d, 'rev-list', 'HEAD')) == 1; assert git(d, 'rev-parse', 'origin/main') == parentHead('main'); commit on main in the parent; git(d, 'fetch', 'origin'); assert git(d, 'rev-parse', 'origin/main') == parentHead('main'); git(d, 'fetch', 'origin', 'refs/parley/changes/7/1'); assert git(d, 'rev-parse', 'FETCH_HEAD') == parentRef('refs/parley/changes/7/1'); ev = events(type='parley.git.fetch', workspace='demo--t1'); assert ev[0].actor_type == 'pat' and ev[0].metadata == {shallow: true, filter: 'blob:none'}; code, err = git('ls-remote', parentURL(pat)); assert code != 0; assert err contains 'repository not found'
